boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Waynesboro record (March 2, 1865) in Sheridan's Expedition to Petersburg [March 1865]. The expedition's march from Winchester to White House (February 27-March 19) and its totals of prisoners and losses are context; they are not assigned to this record. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen and live force fields read 4,100 (US 2,500; CS 1,600). Sheridan gives the effective force of his two cavalry divisions on February 28 as 503 officers and 9,484 men (9,987), and says Custer's division led the attack against Early's two infantry brigades and some cavalry under Rosser; Pond gives 10,000 sabres, Custer's division 4,840 and Devin's 5,047 aggregate effective, against Wharton's two brigades, Nelson's battalion of six guns and Rosser's cavalry.
claims.rationale: The frozen figures state no date or population; the frozen Confederate 1,600 equals the prisoner count both accounts give, an observation only. Sheridan's and Pond's Union figures are the whole expedition's effective strength at the start, not the troops engaged; the Confederate side is by formation. None is adopted as a matched opening strength; live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: Sheridan says he decided to fight Early and directed Custer's division to take up the pursuit, and that Custer made his dispositions at once, sending three regiments around the enemy's left; Pond says the same and that Early and the other Confederate generals fled into the woods. The frozen commanders are Early (CS, Lieutenant General) and Sheridan (US); the live page lists Sheridan and 'Major General Jubal Early'.
claims.rationale: Custer, not a frozen commander, directed the attack in both accounts; Early's own dispositions are not described beyond his position. The live rank is not adopted. No listed commander receives automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. Sheridan says the works were carried and the enemy threw down their arms and surrendered; Pond says the position was carried in an instant and the victory left Sheridan master of the Valley. NPS says the attack rolled up Early's right flank, while Sheridan and Pond put the turning column on his left.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The flank named by NPS conflicts with both inspected accounts; not reconciled.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 1,800 total and the live field 1,630 (US 30; CS 1,600); NPS says more than 1,500 surrendered. Sheridan gives the results as 11 guns, about 200 wagons, 17 battle-flags and 1,600 officers and men, and elsewhere about 1,600 prisoners and not over 100 men lost for the whole march; Pond gives little if any loss on either side, seventeen flags, eleven guns (five found in the town) and 'first and last, about 1,600 officers and men'.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Sheridan's two 1,600 figures (Waynesborough and the whole march) and Pond's 'first and last' may count the same prisoners on different scopes; the march-wide loss is not assigned to this record.

open_questions: Custer's, Merritt's and Devin's reports (Expedition Nos. 8, 3, 4), Lee's dispatches (No. 13), Hotchkiss's journal (No. 14), Early's own account (no report found in the inspected report list) and the returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Pond's The Shenandoah Valley in 1864 (1883) is a retrospective history by a non-participant that, for Waynesboro, quotes and closely follows Sheridan's report, so it is not independent of that family. Sheridan's July 16, 1865 report, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XLVI, Part 1, is an interested commander's account; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
